input.question: Would a suction cup still have the ability to stick to a surface in a vacuum?
input.ground_truth: When a suction cup is pressed against a surface, it pushes out all of the air beneath it and creates a vacuum between the cup and the surface. This vacuum holds the suction cup tightly, and it will continue to do so until the pressure on the outside of the cup becomes lower than the pressure on the inside of the cup. (from [ehow](_URL_0_)) In a vacuum, the pressure outside will be the same as the pressure outside, so no, it will not stick to a surface.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Would a suction cup still have the ability to stick to a surface in a vacuum?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a suction cup, like the kind you see on the wall in cartoons. Normally, when you press it against a wall, air tries to get out from under the cup, but it can’t because the air is stuck there. That’s what helps the suction cup stick.

But in a vacuum, there’s no air at all. So when you try to stick the suction cup to the wall, there’s nothing pushing it against the wall. There’s no air to “hold” it there. That’s why the suction cup can’t stick in a vacuum.

So, in a vacuum, the suction cup loses its “sticky power” because there’s no air to help it stick!
